TASK: Upgrade the Route Optimization Module to an Industry-Level Emergency Navigation System

I want to upgrade ONLY the existing Route Optimization feature of my AI-Driven Disaster Management System.

IMPORTANT:
- Do NOT redesign the entire project.
- Do NOT modify authentication, database schema (unless absolutely necessary), AI analysis engine, resource management, disaster management, rescue teams, notifications, analytics, or any unrelated modules.
- Keep all existing functionality working.
- Extend and improve the current Route Optimization feature only.

Current implementation:
- Uses Haversine (straight-line) distance.
- Calculates basic distance and estimated travel time.
- Does not consider roads, traffic, road closures, or alternate routes.

I want the Route Optimization module to become an enterprise-grade emergency routing system.

Requirements:

1. Replace Straight-Line Routing
- Replace Haversine-only routing with real road routing.
- Use OpenRouteService API (preferred free option).
- If OpenRouteService is unavailable, provide a clean abstraction so Google Maps Directions API or Mapbox Directions API can be plugged in later.
- Keep Haversine only as a fallback when the routing API is unavailable.

2. Real Road Distance
Instead of:
- Straight-line distance

Calculate:
- Actual road distance
- Road travel time
- Route geometry (polyline)
- Turn-by-turn route information

3. Traffic-Aware ETA
If the selected routing provider supports traffic:
- Calculate estimated arrival time considering traffic.
- Display:
  - Normal travel time
  - Current estimated travel time
  - Delay caused by traffic

If traffic is unavailable:
- Clearly indicate that standard routing is being used.

4. Alternate Routes
Generate multiple possible routes.

Display:
- Fastest route
- Shortest route
- Alternative route

Each route should include:
- Distance
- Estimated travel time
- Number of turns
- Route summary

Allow users to select a preferred route.

5. Road Closure Support
Allow roads to be marked as:
- Closed
- Blocked
- Flooded
- Landslide
- Accident

The routing engine should avoid blocked roads whenever possible.

Provide a clean service interface so real road closure data can be integrated later.

6. Multiple Destination Optimization
Allow a rescue team to visit multiple locations efficiently.

Example:
Disaster Area
↓
Hospital
↓
Shelter
↓
Resource Warehouse

Optimize the visit order to minimize total travel distance and time.

A heuristic optimization algorithm is acceptable.

7. Route Visualization
Improve the map by displaying:
- Colored route lines
- Route start marker
- Destination marker
- Intermediate waypoints
- Selected route highlighting

Maintain compatibility with the existing Leaflet/OpenStreetMap implementation.

8. Emergency Route Priority
Add an option:
Emergency Mode

When enabled:
- Prefer main roads
- Minimize travel time
- Avoid blocked roads
- Prioritize emergency vehicle routing where supported

9. Route Details Panel
Show:
- Total distance
- Estimated travel time
- Average speed
- Traffic status
- Number of waypoints
- Route status
- Last updated time

10. Backend Improvements
Create a dedicated Route Optimization Service.

Responsibilities:
- Call the routing provider
- Parse responses
- Handle errors
- Cache recent route results when appropriate
- Fall back to Haversine if the API fails

Keep controllers clean by placing routing logic inside the service layer.

11. Frontend Improvements
Enhance the existing Route Optimization page without redesigning the application.

Include:
- Better route cards
- Route comparison
- Loading indicators
- Error handling
- Refresh route button
- Clear route button

12. API Design
Keep the existing endpoint if possible.

If additional endpoints are needed, add them without breaking compatibility.

13. Code Quality
- Follow the existing project architecture.
- Maintain separation of Controller → Service → Repository.
- Use DTOs where appropriate.
- Write clean, maintainable code.
- Avoid breaking existing functionality.

14. Deliverables
After implementation:
- Explain every new feature added.
- List all modified files.
- List any new dependencies.
- Document any required API keys.
- Verify that the project builds successfully.

## Route Optimization → Enterprise Emergency Navigation System

### 1. Every new feature added

**Backend**
- **Real road routing (Req 1 & 2):** New `OpenRouteServiceProvider` calls the ORS Directions API, returning actual road distance, road travel time, decoded route geometry (polyline), and turn-by-turn instructions per segment. Haversine is retained purely as the offline fallback via `HaversineRouteProvider`.
- **Provider abstraction (Req 1):** New `RouteProvider` interface. `GoogleMapsDirectionsProvider` (traffic-capable) and `MapboxDirectionsProvider` (polyline6-capable) are ready stubs — set `app.routing.provider=google|mapbox` + a key and implement `calculateRoutes()` to plug them in.
- **Traffic-aware ETA (Req 3):** New `TrafficInfo` DTO (`available`, normal/current time, delay, level, message). Providers without live traffic (ORS/Haversine) return `available=false` and the UI clearly shows **"Standard routing in use"**. A Google provider (which supports traffic) will automatically populate real current-ETA vs normal-ETA and delay.
- **Alternate routes (Req 4):** ORS returns up to 4 alternatives (`alternative_routes`); Haversine synthesizes Fastest / Shortest / Alternative (geometrically different) so comparison works offline too. Each route carries distance, time, turns, summary, geometry and steps.
- **Road closures (Req 5):** `RoadClosureService` (interface + `InMemoryRoadClosureService`) manages CLOSED/BLOCKED/FLOODED/LANDSLIDE/ACCIDENT closures. ORS avoids them via GeoJSON `avoid_polygons` (auto-retries without if rejected); Haversine inserts detour arcs around them. New REST endpoints: `POST/GET /api/routes/closures`, `DELETE /api/routes/closures/{id}`.
- **Multi-destination optimization (Req 6):** `RouteOrderOptimizer` (nearest-neighbour + 2-opt) reorders waypoints to minimize distance/time. New endpoint `POST /api/routes/optimize` returns ordered stops + distance/time savings vs original.
- **Emergency priority (Req 8):** `emergencyMode` forces `fastest` preference, uses emergency speed (55 km/h vs 40), and avoids fords/steps in ORS.
- **Backend service (Req 10):** `RouteOptimizationService` orchestrates providers, closure handling, `RouteCache` (SHA-256 key, TTL 10 min), graceful fallback, and assembles the response. Controller stays thin.
- **API compatibility (Req 12):** Existing `POST /api/routes/calculate` unchanged (same URL, same RBAC `ROUTE_VIEW`); it now returns the richer response. Response still exposes legacy aliases `totalDistance` / `estimatedTime`.

**Frontend**
- **Route visualization (Req 7):** `MapView` now renders colored `Polyline` route layers (selected route highlighted thicker, alternatives dashed), keeps start/destination/waypoint markers, adds gray closure markers, and auto-fits bounds (`fitToRoutes`). Fully backward-compatible (other pages unaffected).
- **Route comparison & selection (Req 4/9):** New "Route Comparison" cards for Fastest/Shortest/Alternative — distance, time, turns, summary, recommended badge, "closures avoided" chip — click to select and highlight; plus turn-by-turn directions list.
- **Route details panel (Req 9):** total distance, est. time, average speed, traffic status chip, turns, waypoint count, provider, route status (OK / Offline fallback / Closures avoided), last-updated time.
- **Controls (Req 11):** Emergency Mode / Avoid Closures / Optimize Order switches, alternate-routes count, Refresh and Clear buttons, loading spinners, error toasts, fallback warning banner.
- **Road closures UI (Req 5/11):** form to report closures (type, lat/lng, radius, name, description) + active-closure list with delete.
- **Optimization UI (Req 6):** "Optimize" button fills the form with the optimal visit order and shows savings.
